claims.claim: Spathis's text-mining comparison of four best-selling series reports that A Song of Ice and Fire lacks -ly adverbs relative to the other three series.
claims.quote: the lack of -ly adverbs in Game of Thrones

claims.claim: Spathis's key-takeaway list states that Game of Thrones contains significantly fewer -ly adverbs than the other series analysed.
claims.quote: significantly fewer -ly adverbs

claims.claim: Spathis's adverb finding is stated only for the -ly suffixed form of the adverb, never for adverbs as a whole class.
claims.quote: significantly fewer -ly adverbs
claims.confidence: medium — the limb rests on the wording of both adverb sentences naming '-ly adverbs'; the page carries no sentence about adverbs in general

claims.claim: Spathis reports no numeric adverb rate in the article's running text; the adverb comparison is carried entirely by a chart image.
claims.confidence: medium — an absence claim; verified against the full text as fetched, in which the only adverb sentences are prose and the figure is an image placeholder

claims.claim: Spathis removed character names, along with very frequent words and phrases, as stopwords before ranking parts of speech.
claims.quote: as well as character names

claims.claim: Spathis's corpus is 3,896,568 words drawn from nineteen books by four authors.
Spathis's Automated Readability Index result places Game of Thrones at the comprehension level of 11-year-olds.
claims.quote: Game of Thrones to 11-year-olds

claims.claim: Spathis reports that Martin's most frequent colour adjectives across the series are red, white and grey.
claims.quote: Notable is the usage of colors by author

claims.claim: Spathis reports that lady and queen are among the most frequent nouns in the Game of Thrones books.
claims.quote: is probably apparent in Game of Thrones

claims.claim: Spathis offers Stephen King's advice against adverbs only as speculation about why Martin's -ly count is low, not as anything Martin said.
claims.quote: Perhaps George Martin follows Stephen King

claims.claim: Spathis reports that the largest books in his four-series analysis score low on lexical density.
claims.quote: the largest books of our analysis behave poorly
